learning: y=0.07 m gave the best s-bend progress but jitter and line loss; y=0.06 m kept the jitter and line loss and lost the s-bend gain. Test whether y=0.05 m removes both while keeping some gain. Check the oval separately, since its progress has not moved since iteration 1.
notes: Applies the pre-agreed rule: sensor row returned from y=0.06 m to 0.05 m, with the controller held at iteration 3/4 settings so the lead change is isolated.
rationale: Iteration 4 (y=0.06 m, 36.81) brought back s-bend line loss (0.9 per run) and slalom steering_oscillation of 0.141, both above the 0.10 threshold. Iteration 3 (y=0.07 m, 51.31) gave the best s-bend progress (0.155). The oval has been fixed at progress 0.115 and max_error 0.061 m since iteration 1, so it does not respond to sensor row position, mass, track width or lead. Following the pre-agreed rule (oscillation above 0.10 at a lead of 0.06 m, return the row to 0.05 m), I accept the Builder's geometry unchanged: sensor row y=0.05 m, x = -0.05 to 0.05 m, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.09 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.5 kg, body 0.12 x 0.12 m. The controller is kept at iteration 3/4 settings (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.10, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]), so this race isolates the lead change. The sensor count and spread match the weights, so the signal stays within about +/-2. Expected: steering_oscillation falls below 0.10 on slalom and s-bend, line_loss_events trends to 0, and the s-bend keeps some progress gain, with the score near or a little below 51. The oval should stay near progress 0.115. wheel_radius is not changed, so the speed test does not confound the lead test.
